original_sql:
SELECT c.c_custkey, c.c_name,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders o WHERE o.o_custkey = c.c_custkey) AS n_orders
FROM customer c
WHERE c.c_nationkey = 7

candidates.sql:
SELECT c.c_custkey, c.c_name, COUNT(o.o_orderkey) AS n_orders
FROM customer c
LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.o_custkey = c.c_custkey
WHERE c.c_nationkey = 7
GROUP BY c.c_custkey, c.c_name
candidates.rationale: Replaces the correlated subquery with a LEFT JOIN and GROUP BY, allowing the optimizer to use a single hash join or merge join instead of executing a subquery for each customer row.

candidates.sql:
SELECT c.c_custkey, c.c_name, COALESCE(o.n_orders, 0) AS n_orders
FROM customer c
LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT o_custkey, COUNT(*) AS n_orders
    FROM orders
    GROUP BY o_custkey
) o ON o.o_custkey = c.c_custkey
WHERE c.c_nationkey = 7
candidates.rationale: Pre-aggregates the orders table in a derived table and then joins it to the filtered customers, reducing the join size and avoiding per-row subquery execution.
